description: Identifier of one query instance.
The query this instance belongs to. All instances of a group share a normal form. Use this to split train and test.
Number of terms in the union of the normal form.
Number of distinct base relations referenced by the normal form.
Number of inner joins in the normal form.
Number of anti-joins and semi-joins, arising from EXCEPT, NOT EXISTS and NOT IN after rules t2 and the EXISTS translation.
Number of selection predicates over base attributes.
Number of aggregate functions computed.
Number of grouping attributes.
Number of ordering attributes.
Maximum nesting depth of normalised subexpressions. 1 for a flat query, 2 when a join operand or an anti-join operand is itself a normal form.
Size class of the largest input relation: small (<=200 MB), medium (<=2000 MB) or large. Encode before use.
Number of input relations over 2000 MB.
Number of input relations at or under 200 MB. Small relations can be held in transient memory, which is what makes a nested-loop join viable.
Fastest tier holding any input relation, 0 to 3.
Slowest tier holding any input relation, 0 to 3.
Total size of all input relations in MB.
Prose description of the query shape. For reading, not for training.
Identifier of one candidate plan.
The query instance this candidate belongs to. Join key to query_features.
The query group. Use this to split train and test.
Prose description of the plan: target tier, partitioning, join algorithm, pipelining. For reading, not for training.
Numeric tag of the strategy that produced this candidate, 1 to 40.
Total number of operations in the plan.
Number of join operations.
Number of selection and subquery-block operations.
Number of aggregation operations.
Number of sort operations, including the extra sorts a sort-merge join requires.
Join algorithm: 0 nested loop, 1 hash, 2 sort merge, 3 index nested loop. Categorical, so one-hot encode for a linear model.
Access method: 0 sequential, 1 index. Categorical.
Number of operations fused into an in-memory pipeline, so their output is never written to storage.
Longest pipeline in the plan, in operations.
Number of operations run on partitioned input.
Largest partition count actually achieved. Capped by the devices at the tier, so an operation on l3 cannot exceed 1.
Volume read and written on tier l0 (HDD) in MB.
Volume read and written on tier l1 (SSD) in MB.
Volume read and written on tier l2 (high-speed SSD) in MB.
Volume read and written on tier l3 (NVMe) in MB.
Number of operations whose read tier differs from its write tier.
Number of operations whose output is written to a faster tier than the one it was read from.
Difference between the slowest and fastest tier the plan touches.
Total volume read from persistent storage in MB, including re-reads of intermediate results.
Total volume written to persistent storage in MB. Lower than the sum of operation outputs when operations are pipelined.
Size of the largest intermediate result in MB. Decides whether an operation can be pipelined or placed on a small fast tier.
Final output size divided by total input size. A property of the query, so constant across the candidates of one instance.
Estimated execution cost from the analytical model, in time units. A regression target; exclude it when predicting which plan wins, or the task is trivial.
This candidate cost divided by the best cost of its instance. 1.0 for the winner.
1 if this candidate is the cheapest of its instance, else 0.
template_id of the cheapest candidate of this instance. The label the framework retrieves.
strategy_tag of the cheapest candidate. Multiclass target.
Identifier of the query instance.
The query group.
Which scale factor produced this instance: SF1, SF3 or SF10. NOT a feature: a query arriving at runtime carries no such label. Its effect reaches the model through input_mb and the size classes.

Which storage placement produced this instance. baseline is the deployed configuration; cold, hot and split are hypothetical variants standing for the same database after data migration. NOT a feature: its effect reaches the model through tier_min, tier_max and the per-tier volumes.
